Chapter 1 · The learner

Meet Pooja.

✓ Completed Class 12 · Agriculture stream

Not a senior scientist. Not a technology expert. A young agriculture learner who wants to understand the farmer's real problems — by standing in the field next to them.

She visits farms, sits with farmers at the bund, and writes down what actually goes wrong in a season:

Crop disease spotted too late
Rising input costs
Irrigation timing
Weather uncertainty
Fertiliser decisions
Pesticide decisions
Volatile mandi prices
Transport costs
No affordable storage
Distress selling at low prices
Scheme access & paperwork
Advice that arrives too late
Language barriers
Apps built for someone else
“Farmers don't need another complicated app. They need simple answers that help them make better decisions.”
India · Diversity is the design constraint

One country. Many farms.

Click a state on the globe. Soil, climate, crop, water, market and language all change — so the same AI engine must give a different answer.

Same AI engine→Local context→Local language→Local crop→Different recommendation

Crop/soil/climate notes are broad, well-established regional characteristics. Language lines are illustrative demo phrases — production content must be reviewed by native-speaking agronomists.

The farmer speaks. The assistant understands.

Farmer speaks→Speech recognition→Agricultural AI→Verified knowledge→Local-language answer→Voice reply

Honest competitive landscape

The market is already being validated.

Government of India · 2026

Bharat-VISTAAR

Launched 17 Feb 2026 in Jaipur as a voice-first, multilingual AI platform (Digital Public Infrastructure). Phase 1 integrates IMD weather, AgMarkNet mandi prices, National Pest Surveillance System inputs, Agri-Stack data and 10 central schemes; reachable via helpline 155261 — even on feature phones. Hindi & English first, more languages planned.

Govt of Maharashtra · 2025

MahaVISTAAR-AI

Launched 21 May 2025 with the World Bank-assisted PoCRA project. Voice chat in Marathi and local languages; weather forecasts, crop advisories, pest guidance, market rates and government services. Reported to have crossed 10 lakh downloads statewide (June 2026).

NGO · India / Africa

Farmer.Chat (Digital Green)

Generative-AI assistant over vetted extension content; text, voice and photo queries in languages including Hindi, Telugu and Bhojpuri, also on WhatsApp.

Private · Germany / India

Plantix

Photo-based diagnosis of crop diseases, pests and nutrient deficiencies — proof that “take a photo” is a familiar farmer workflow.

Private · India

Kissan AI

Voice-based agricultural chatbot, launched as KissanGPT in March 2023.

Buyer & service ecosystem

From information chatbot to decision & business layer.

Once the farmer trusts the decisions, the next step is acting on them — finding a buyer, booking a tractor, cold storage or a soil test.

Future ecosystem capability

Not part of the first MVP. Built only after diagnosis, market and profit features are validated with farmers.

“We do not need to train a massive AI model from scratch.”

Existing foundation models + domain RAG over verified agricultural knowledge + specialised crop models + Indian-language voice (e.g., Bhashini / AI4Bharat building blocks).

Small AI

Design for the field, not the lab.

High-end AI lab

  • Big models, fast networks
  • English-first interfaces
  • Experts type long prompts

The actual design target

  • Entry-level Android or feature phone
  • 2G/3G or patchy 4G; voice call fallback
  • Speak, don't type; local language
  • Small on-device model for common diseases, cloud for the rest
  • Answers in under a minute, in one screen

Precedent: PlantVillage Nuru ran cassava disease detection offline on phones (Ramcharan et al., 2017 & later work).

AI + agriculture + sustainability

A wider circular economy — later.

These connections are not forced into the farmer's daily workflow. They sketch a future ecosystem where AI could help optimise resources: solar pumps, batteries, agricultural and electronic waste, water and materials.

Future Research & Commercial Opportunities

Bhavira Technologies connection

Potential links with Bhavira's expertise in electrochemistry, resource recovery, sustainable materials and solar / e-waste / circular economy:

  • Recovery of valuable metals from agricultural & electronic waste streams
  • Recycling of solar-panel materials from farm solar installations
  • Battery material recovery (solar pump & storage batteries)
  • Resource-efficient agricultural infrastructure
  • AI-assisted circular-resource management

Not commercial products. Research directions to be explored and validated.
